contentBlocks.text: What to know about June payments

Youth Day fell on Tuesday 16 June, comfortably between the permanent-grant window and the SRD batches, so no pay date moved. Collections in the first week proceeded normally at cards, banks and retail tills.

June also marked the mid-year point for SRD income re-verifications. Beneficiaries whose UIF or income data triggered flags saw 'referred' or 'under review' statuses during the month; resolving these before the July review cycle kept payments uninterrupted.

Practical winter tip: cold mornings make long queues harder for older beneficiaries. If your grant lands early in the month, consider collecting from the second or third day after payday — balances do not disappear by waiting.

faqs.question: What are the SASSA payment dates for June 2026?
faqs.answer: Older Persons grants were paid on Wednesday 3 June 2026, Disability grants on Thursday 4 June, Children's grants on Friday 5 June, and SRD R370 payments ran from 25 to 30 June.

faqs.question: Did Youth Day affect June payments?
faqs.answer: No. Youth Day fell on Tuesday 16 June 2026, which was neither a permanent-grant pay date nor a disruption to the SRD batch schedule.

faqs.question: My SRD status changed to referred in June. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: 'Referred' means SASSA's system flagged your file for extra verification — often income data. Follow the instructions in your SMS or visit an office; unresolved referrals eventually lead to declines.

faqs.question: Is there enough time to collect my June money before month-end?
faqs.answer: Yes. Grant money remains available indefinitely — collecting days or even weeks after the official date has no effect on the amount.
